    11. Case Study: The Kotlin Client for the RdvMedecins Application

    11.1. The Problem

    The [RdvMedecins] application allows users to schedule appointments at a doctor's office. The [NestJS] course developed it as a HTML application, in which the server generated the pages; the courses [Vue.js], [Angular], and [React] developed web clients for it, and the [Flutter] course created a mobile client, which generates the SAME screens from the JSON data provided by the server described in the chapter “The RdvMedecins Server: A Black Box.” This chapter describes how to write a native [Android] client, in [Kotlin] and [Jetpack Compose].

    The client must provide everything the others provided:

    • a login screen, protected by a CAPTCHA, with the option to create a patient account;
    • a doctor’s schedule for a given day, with appointment booking (patient selection window) and cancellation;
    • for the administrator, management of doctors and clients (list, add, edit, delete);
    • for the patient, a personal dashboard (showing upcoming appointments, which they can cancel) and account management;
    • two languages: French and English;
    • the same screens as the web clients ([/login], [/schedule], [/doctors], [/my-area]...), which here become ROUTES navigation screens.

    A mobile app adds its own requirements: a narrow screen (no five-column tables), a keyboard that hides half the screen, a Back button, screen rotation and language switching that affect the activity (they RECREATE it), a password manager, and the absence of a browser to store the token cookie.

    11.2. Installation and Execution

    The JSON server must be installed and running (see the chapter “The RdvMedecins Server: A Black Box”). The CAPTCHA test mode is not required: you can leave [CAPTCHA_TEST] empty in the server’s [.env] file.

    In [Android Studio], [File / Open] opens the [rdvmedecins_kotlin] folder; [Gradle] downloads the libraries (the first time, this takes a few minutes). Once the emulator is running, a command window connects its port 8080 to the computer’s port:

    1
    adb reverse tcp:8080 tcp:8080

    then the [Run] button installs and launches the application. You can also do everything in a command window opened to the [rdvmedecins_kotlin] folder:

    1
2
3
    gradlew installDebug
gradlew installDebug -Pserver=http://10.0.2.2:8080
gradlew installDebug -Pserver=http://192.168.1.20:8080
    • The first line compiles and installs the application on the connected device (emulator or phone), which connects to the server at the address [http://localhost:8080] using [adb reverse];
    • the second, for the emulator, without [adb reverse]: the emulator sees the computer at the address [10.0.2.2];
    • the third, for a real phone connected via Wi-Fi to the same network as the computer: we provide the computer’s address on that network ([ipconfig] under [Windows]); the firewall on [Windows] must allow incoming connections on port 8080. A phone connected to USB (with “USB debugging” enabled in its developer options) can also use [adb reverse].

    Demo accounts are listed on the login screen (password = login).

    11.3. Using the App

    The screenshots in this section are from a Pixel 8 emulator (1080 × 2400 pixels, 412 × 915 dp). They were generated automatically by an instrumented test ([app/src/androidTest/.../CaseStudyCaptures.kt], see appendices) that navigates the app as a user would.

    11.3.1. The login screen

    The login screen; incorrect password: the message appears at the bottom of the screen, and a new image is displayed (each image is used only once):

    11.3.2. The schedule, as seen by the administrator and doctors

    Logged in as [admin], you arrive at the calendar. Select a doctor and a day (the day, from a calendar), then “View schedule”:

    “Book” opens the booking window, with a navigation path displayed over the calendar; the appointment is saved; “Cancel” prompts for confirmation:

    A doctor ([pelissier]) is taken directly to THEIR daily calendar:

    11.3.3. The Patient’s Area

    A patient ([martin]) accesses “My area.” In a calendar, they book an appointment for themselves without selecting a patient:

    Their appointment appears under their name; the “Book” button is no longer available (only one upcoming appointment), and a message explains why. Their account shows the appointment. “Manage my account”: any changes require the current password; errors are server-related:

    A patient’s menu does not have a “Doctors” entry. If they were to open this screen anyway (via a link), the navigation would display a 403 error page (see [navigation/Navigation.kt]).

    11.3.4. Managing Doctors and Clients

    The list of doctors; an incorrectly filled-out addition; a successful addition:

    A duplicate entry; a successful deletion:

    11.3.5. Creating an Account

    On the login screen, enter the CAPTCHA and then tap “Create a patient account.” The form is rejected by the server; once the account is created, return to the login screen, where the login information is pre-filled:

    11.3.6. In French, then on a large screen

    The FR / EN menu in the top bar changes the application’s language: the activity is recreated, and EVERYTHING is re-translated, including the calendar and dates. On a wide screen (a tablet or a phone held horizontally), the menu remains displayed on the left:

    11.3.7. Session expired

    If the token expires (or if the cookie is deleted), the next request returns a 401; the application redirects to the login screen. After logging in, it will redirect the user back to the screen they wanted to view:

    rdvmedecins_kotlin/
├── settings.gradle.kts, build.gradle.kts    the Gradle project
├── gradle/libs.versions.toml               the versions of the libraries
└── app/
    ├── build.gradle.kts                    the module of the application
    └── src/
        ├── androidTest/                    the test that makes the screenshots
        └── main/
            ├── AndroidManifest.xml
            ├── assets/i18n/                the dictionaries fr.json, en.json
            ├── res/                        icon, name, theme, languages
            └── java/fr/stahe/rdvmedecins/
                ├── RdvMedecinsApplication.kt  the shared objects
                ├── MainActivity.kt         the single activity
                ├── Config.kt               the address of the server
                ├── Formatting.kt           hours and days
                ├── api/                    the API access layer
                ├── state/                  session, messages, cache
                ├── i18n/                   the languages
                ├── navigation/             the screens, their routes, their access rights
                ├── widgets/                the layout and the reusable components
                └── pages/                  the screens

    This is the architecture recommended by the [Android] guide (“Guide to App Architecture”), simplified as follows:

    • a data layer ([api/]): the only layer that knows about [OkHttp], the URL objects, and the JSON object;
    • a state layer ([state/]): objects whose properties are [Compose] states, created once by the [Application] object and provided to all screens ([LocalDependencies]);
    • an interface layer ([pages/], [widgets/]): functions [@Composable], which display the state and transmit user actions.

    The following table compares the HTML application from the [NestJS] course, the [Flutter] client, and this client:

    Application HTML (NestJS)
    Flutter client
    Kotlin client
    The server renders each page ([res.render])
    Widgets render the screens
    Functions [@Composable] generate the screens
    [views/layout.hbs] and its partial views
    [layout.dart] (a [ShellRoute])
    [AppLayout.kt], around [NavHost]
    the controller routes
    [go_router]
    [navigation-compose], routes [@Serializable]
    [JwtAuthGuard], [RolesGuard]
    The [redirect] function of the router
    [Protected] and an effect that observes the session
    the token cookie, stored by the browser
    a client HTTP that manages cookies
    the [CookieJar] from [OkHttp]
    Flash message in a cookie
    a [ChangeNotifier], [Messages]
    a stateful class [Compose], [Messages]
    Dictionaries read by the server
    [Translations] (JSON)
    [Translations] (SAME JSON files)
    language stored in a cookie
    in [shared_preferences]
    by [Android] ([setApplicationLocales])
    data that has already been read
    [Cache] (a few lines)
    [Cache] (a few lines, from [Deferred])
    Form rejected: the server reloads the page
    400/409 response, errors below the fields
    same

    // =========================================================================
// settings.gradle.kts - the GLOBAL configuration of the Gradle project
// (generated by Android Studio; only rootProject.name has been changed)
// =========================================================================

// where Gradle looks for its PLUGINS (the Android plugin, the Compose plugin...)
pluginManagement {
    repositories {
        google {
            content {
                includeGroupByRegex("com\\.android.*")
                includeGroupByRegex("com\\.google.*")
                includeGroupByRegex("androidx.*")
            }
        }
        mavenCentral()
        gradlePluginPortal()
    }
}
plugins {
    id("org.gradle.toolchains.foojay-resolver-convention") version "1.0.0"
}
// where Gradle looks for the LIBRARIES: google() for AndroidX and Compose,
// mavenCentral() for OkHttp, kotlinx.serialization, AndroidSVG
dependencyResolutionManagement {
    repositoriesMode.set(RepositoriesMode.FAIL_ON_PROJECT_REPOS)
    repositories {
        google()
        mavenCentral()
    }
}

rootProject.name = "rdvmedecins_kotlin"
// a single module: the application, in the app/ folder
include(":app")
// =========================================================================
// build.gradle.kts (root) - declares the Gradle plugins used by the
// modules of the project, without applying them here ("apply false"): it is
// app/build.gradle.kts that applies them.
// =========================================================================
plugins {
    alias(libs.plugins.android.application) apply false
    alias(libs.plugins.kotlin.compose) apply false
    alias(libs.plugins.kotlin.serialization) apply false
}

    # =========================================================================
# gradle/libs.versions.toml - the "version catalog" of the project
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ALL the versions of the plugins and of the libraries, in one single place.
# The build.gradle.kts files refer to them by names
# (libs.okhttp, libs.plugins.kotlin.compose...). It is the equivalent of the
# dependencies section of Flutter's pubspec.yaml.
# =========================================================================

[versions]
agp = "9.4.1"
kotlin = "2.2.10"
coreKtx = "1.17.0"
lifecycle = "2.9.4"
activityCompose = "1.11.0"
composeBom = "2026.02.01"
appcompat = "1.7.1"
navigation = "2.9.5"
okhttp = "4.12.0"
kotlinxSerializationJson = "1.9.0"
androidsvg = "1.4"
junit = "4.13.2"
junitVersion = "1.3.0"
espressoCore = "3.7.0"
testRunner = "1.7.0"

[libraries]
# --- generated by Android Studio ("Empty Activity" template) ---
androidx-core-ktx = { group = "androidx.core", name = "core-ktx", version.ref = "coreKtx" }
androidx-lifecycle-runtime-ktx = { group = "androidx.lifecycle", name = "lifecycle-runtime-ktx", version.ref = "lifecycle" }
androidx-activity-compose = { group = "androidx.activity", name = "activity-compose", version.ref = "activityCompose" }
androidx-compose-bom = { group = "androidx.compose", name = "compose-bom", version.ref = "composeBom" }
androidx-compose-ui = { group = "androidx.compose.ui", name = "ui" }
androidx-compose-ui-graphics = { group = "androidx.compose.ui", name = "ui-graphics" }
androidx-compose-ui-tooling = { group = "androidx.compose.ui", name = "ui-tooling" }
androidx-compose-ui-tooling-preview = { group = "androidx.compose.ui", name = "ui-tooling-preview" }
androidx-compose-ui-test-manifest = { group = "androidx.compose.ui", name = "ui-test-manifest" }
androidx-compose-ui-test-junit4 = { group = "androidx.compose.ui", name = "ui-test-junit4" }
androidx-compose-material3 = { group = "androidx.compose.material3", name = "material3" }
junit = { group = "junit", name = "junit", version.ref = "junit" }
androidx-junit = { group = "androidx.test.ext", name = "junit", version.ref = "junitVersion" }
androidx-espresso-core = { group = "androidx.test.espresso", name = "espresso-core", version.ref = "espressoCore" }
androidx-test-runner = { group = "androidx.test", name = "runner", version.ref = "testRunner" }
# --- added for RdvMedecins ---
# the basic Material icons (Add, Delete, Search...)
androidx-compose-material-icons-core = { group = "androidx.compose.material", name = "material-icons-core" }
# the activity's lifecycle seen from Compose 
androidx-lifecycle-runtime-compose = { group = "androidx.lifecycle", name = "lifecycle-runtime-compose", version.ref = "lifecycle" }
# viewModel() in a @Composable function 
androidx-lifecycle-viewmodel-compose = { group = "androidx.lifecycle", name = "lifecycle-viewmodel-compose", version.ref = "lifecycle" }
# the application's OWN language 
androidx-appcompat = { group = "androidx.appcompat", name = "appcompat", version.ref = "appcompat" }
# the router 
androidx-navigation-compose = { group = "androidx.navigation", name = "navigation-compose", version.ref = "navigation" }
# the HTTP client 
okhttp = { group = "com.squareup.okhttp3", name = "okhttp", version.ref = "okhttp" }
# JSON (de)serialization 
kotlinx-serialization-json = { group = "org.jetbrains.kotlinx", name = "kotlinx-serialization-json", version.ref = "kotlinxSerializationJson" }
# drawing an SVG image (the captcha)
androidsvg = { group = "com.caverock", name = "androidsvg-aar", version.ref = "androidsvg" }

[plugins]
android-application = { id = "com.android.application", version.ref = "agp" }
kotlin-compose = { id = "org.jetbrains.kotlin.plugin.compose", version.ref = "kotlin" }
# generates the (de)serialization code of the @Serializable classes
kotlin-serialization = { id = "org.jetbrains.kotlin.plugin.serialization", version.ref = "kotlin" }

    The libraries from the examples, except for [DataStore]: the language is stored by [Android] itself, and the token is stored in the cookie jar.

    // =========================================================================
// app/build.gradle.kts - the configuration of the "app" module: the
// RdvMedecins Android client. Generated by Android Studio ("Empty
// Activity" template), then completed (lines marked "added").
// =========================================================================
plugins {
    alias(libs.plugins.android.application)
    alias(libs.plugins.kotlin.compose)
    // added: the kotlinx.serialization plugin (@Serializable classes)
    alias(libs.plugins.kotlin.serialization)
}

android {
    namespace = "fr.stahe.rdvmedecins"
    compileSdk {
        version = release(37)
    }

    defaultConfig {
        applicationId = "fr.stahe.rdvmedecins"
        minSdk = 26
        targetSdk = 37
        versionCode = 1
        versionName = "1.0"
        // added: the address of the JSON server, can be changed at compile time:
        //     gradlew installDebug -Pserver=http://192.168.1.20:8080
        val server = providers.gradleProperty("server").getOrElse("http://localhost:8080")
        buildConfigField("String", "SERVER_URL", "\"$server\"")

        testInstrumentationRunner = "androidx.test.runner.AndroidJUnitRunner"
    }

    buildTypes {
        release {
            optimization {
                enable = false
            }
        }
    }
    compileOptions {
        sourceCompatibility = JavaVersion.VERSION_11
        targetCompatibility = JavaVersion.VERSION_11
    }
    buildFeatures {
        compose = true
        // added: the BuildConfig class (BuildConfig.SERVER_URL)
        buildConfig = true
    }
}

dependencies {

    <?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!-- =====================================================================
     AndroidManifest.xml - the "identity card" of the application
     ===================================================================== -->
<manifest xmlns:android="http://schemas.android.com/apk/res/android"
    xmlns:tools="http://schemas.android.com/tools">

    <!-- network access (the JSON server) -->
    <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.INTERNET" />

    <!-- android:name: the Application class (RdvMedecinsApplication.kt).
         usesCleartextTraffic: the "cleartext" HTTP of the development server
         (to be removed for a production server in https, see Deployment).
         localeConfig: the languages offered by the application -->
    <application
        android:name=".RdvMedecinsApplication"
        android:allowBackup="true"
        android:dataExtractionRules="@xml/data_extraction_rules"
        android:fullBackupContent="@xml/backup_rules"
        android:icon="@mipmap/ic_launcher"
        android:label="@string/app_name"
        android:localeConfig="@xml/locales_config"
        android:roundIcon="@mipmap/ic_launcher_round"
        android:supportsRtl="true"
        android:theme="@style/Theme.RdvMedecins"
        android:usesCleartextTraffic="true"
        tools:targetApi="33">

        <!-- the only activity. windowSoftInputMode="adjustResize": the
             keyboard shrinks the screen instead of hiding it -->
        <activity
            android:name=".MainActivity"
            android:exported="true"
            android:windowSoftInputMode="adjustResize">
            <intent-filter>
                <action android:name="android.intent.action.MAIN" />
                <category android:name="android.intent.category.LAUNCHER" />
            </intent-filter>
        </activity>

        <!-- before Android 13: AppCompat remembers the chosen language -->
        <service
            android:name="androidx.appcompat.app.AppLocalesMetadataHolderService"
            android:enabled="false"
            android:exported="false">
            <meta-data
                android:name="autoStoreLocales"
                android:value="true" />
        </service>
    </application>

</manifest>
    • a single activity, [MainActivity]: all screens are functions of [@Composable];
    • [windowSoftInputMode="adjustResize"]: when the keyboard appears, the screen shrinks (instead of being hidden by the keyboard);
    • [android:localeConfig] and the service for [AppCompat]: the application-specific language (see Example 21).

    // =========================================================================
// RdvMedecinsApplication.kt - the objects shared by the whole application
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Android creates ONE Application object at launch, before any activity, and
// keeps it until the application stops. There we build, once and
// for all, the objects shared by all the screens:
//   - the HTTP client (and its cookie jar), the API access layer;
//   - the session (who is logged in?), the messages, the data cache.
// They thus survive the recreation of the activity (rotation, change
// of language). The screens get them through LocalDependencies (see
// MainActivity.kt): it is a hand-written "dependency injection".
// Two mechanisms connect these objects together:
//   1. the 401 response to a protected request (expired session): the user
//      is forgotten and the message is prepared; the navigation, which observes
//      the session, then goes back to the login screen;
//   2. a change of user: the data read for the previous user
//      are worth nothing any more, the cache is cleared.
// =========================================================================
package fr.stahe.rdvmedecins

import android.app.Application
import androidx.compose.runtime.snapshotFlow
import androidx.compose.runtime.staticCompositionLocalOf
import fr.stahe.rdvmedecins.api.ApiClient
import fr.stahe.rdvmedecins.api.RdvMedecinsApi
import fr.stahe.rdvmedecins.api.createHttpClient
import fr.stahe.rdvmedecins.state.Cache
import fr.stahe.rdvmedecins.state.Messages
import fr.stahe.rdvmedecins.state.Session
import kotlinx.coroutines.MainScope
import kotlinx.coroutines.launch

class RdvMedecinsApplication : Application() {
    // a coroutine scope that lives as long as the application
    val scope = MainScope()
    lateinit var api: RdvMedecinsApi
        private set
    lateinit var session: Session
        private set
    val messages = Messages()
    val cache = Cache(scope)

    override fun onCreate() {
        super.onCreate()
        val client = ApiClient(createHttpClient(this))
        api = RdvMedecinsApi(client)
        session = Session(api)
        // 1. the expired session
        client.onSessionExpired = {
            session.forget()
            messages.flash("ERRORS.SESSION_EXPIRED", success = false)
        }
        // 2. the user changes: snapshotFlow turns a Compose state into a Flow
        scope.launch {
            snapshotFlow { session.user }.collect { cache.clear() }
        }
    }
}

// the Application object, provided to all the screens
val LocalDependencies = staticCompositionLocalOf<RdvMedecinsApplication> { error("no dependencies provided") }
    • Lines 35–41: shared objects, created once. [lateinit var]: a non-[null] property, initialized later (in [onCreate]); [MainScope()]: a coroutine scope that lives as long as the application;
    • lines 49–51: the session has expired: the function entrusted to the API client (which knows nothing else) forgets the user and prepares the message;
    • line 55: [snapshotFlow] transforms a [Compose] state into a [Flow] state (see Example 19): every time the user changes, the cache is cleared;
    • line 61: the object [Application], supplied to all screens by a [CompositionLocal] (see Example 14): a hand-coded “dependency injection.”

    // =========================================================================
// MainActivity.kt - the only activity of the application
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// All the screens are @Composable functions, displayed by the NavHost
// (see navigation/Navigation.kt) in THIS activity. It provides to all
// the screens (CompositionLocalProvider):
//   - the shared objects of the application (LocalDependencies);
//   - the translations of the current language (LocalTranslations).
// It is an AppCompatActivity: it knows how to apply the language chosen by
// the user (see example 21), even before Android 13.
// =========================================================================
package fr.stahe.rdvmedecins

import android.os.Bundle
import androidx.activity.compose.setContent
import androidx.activity.enableEdgeToEdge
import androidx.appcompat.app.AppCompatActivity
import androidx.compose.material3.MaterialTheme
import androidx.compose.material3.lightColorScheme
import androidx.compose.runtime.CompositionLocalProvider
import androidx.compose.ui.graphics.Color
import fr.stahe.rdvmedecins.i18n.LocalTranslations
import fr.stahe.rdvmedecins.i18n.rememberTranslations
import fr.stahe.rdvmedecins.navigation.Navigation

// the colors: the blue of the other RdvMedecins clients (Bootstrap)
private val colors = lightColorScheme(
    primary = Color(0xFF0D6EFD),
    onPrimary = Color.White,
    primaryContainer = Color(0xFFD8E2FF),
    onPrimaryContainer = Color(0xFF001A41),
    secondaryContainer = Color(0xFFDAE2F9),
    onSecondaryContainer = Color(0xFF131C2B),
    surface = Color(0xFFFAF9FD),
)

class MainActivity : AppCompatActivity() {
    override fun onCreate(savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
        super.onCreate(savedInstanceState)
        enableEdgeToEdge()
        val dependencies = application as RdvMedecinsApplication
        setContent {
            MaterialTheme(colorScheme = colors) {
                CompositionLocalProvider(
                    LocalDependencies provides dependencies,
                    LocalTranslations provides rememberTranslations(),
                ) {
                    Navigation()
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

    // =========================================================================
// Formatting.kt - the display of times and days
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The server sends RAW data (startHour: 8, startMinute: 0; day:
// "2026-10-05"); the formatting, which depends on the language, is the business
// of the client (see example 09).
// =========================================================================
package fr.stahe.rdvmedecins

import fr.stahe.rdvmedecins.api.Slot
import fr.stahe.rdvmedecins.api.ScheduleSlot
import java.time.Instant
import java.time.LocalDate
import java.time.ZoneOffset
import java.time.format.DateTimeFormatter
import java.time.format.FormatStyle
import java.util.Locale

// "8:05" rather than "8:5"
fun time(h: Int, m: Int) = "$h:${m.toString().padStart(2, '0')}"

// "8:00 - 8:20"
fun timeRange(c: Slot) = "${time(c.startHour, c.startMinute)} - ${time(c.endHour, c.endMinute)}"
fun timeRange(c: ScheduleSlot) = "${time(c.startHour, c.startMinute)} - ${time(c.endHour, c.endMinute)}"

fun today(): String = LocalDate.now().toString() // "yyyy-MM-dd", the format of the API

// true if day is a date that exists, in the yyyy-MM-dd format ("2026-02-30": no)
fun isValidDate(day: String): Boolean =
    Regex("^\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}$").matches(day) && runCatching { LocalDate.parse(day) }.isSuccess

// "lundi 5 octobre 2026" / "Monday, October 5, 2026"
fun longDate(day: String, language: String): String =
    LocalDate.parse(day).format(DateTimeFormatter.ofLocalizedDate(FormatStyle.FULL).withLocale(Locale.forLanguageTag(language)))

// the Material calendar works in milliseconds (UTC)
fun toMillis(day: String): Long = LocalDate.parse(day).atStartOfDay(ZoneOffset.UTC).toInstant().toEpochMilli()
fun fromMillis(ms: Long): String = Instant.ofEpochMilli(ms).atZone(ZoneOffset.UTC).toLocalDate().toString()

    The server sends RAW data ([startHour: 8], [day: "2026-10-05"]): their formatting, which depends on the language, is the client’s responsibility (see Example 09).

    // =========================================================================
// api/HttpClient.kt - an HTTP client that handles COOKIES
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Taken from example 23 (common/HttpClient.kt). The RdvMedecins server
// puts the JWT token in an httpOnly cookie. On a phone, there is no
// browser to keep it: it is the "cookie jar" (CookieJar) of the
// OkHttp client that stores it, and sends it back with each request. The
// cookies are also stored on the device (SharedPreferences): we stay
// logged in when we stop then restart the application.
// Two cookies travel: the token (rdvmedecins_jwt, path /api) and the
// account-creation pass (path /api/register).
// =========================================================================
package fr.stahe.rdvmedecins.api

import android.content.Context
import android.content.SharedPreferences
import androidx.core.content.edit
import fr.stahe.rdvmedecins.Config
import okhttp3.Cookie
import okhttp3.CookieJar
import okhttp3.HttpUrl
import okhttp3.HttpUrl.Companion.toHttpUrl
import okhttp3.OkHttpClient
import java.util.concurrent.TimeUnit

class DeviceCookieJar(private val storage: SharedPreferences) : CookieJar {
    // cookie name -> the cookie
    private val cookies = mutableMapOf<String, Cookie>()

    init {
        // the cookies remembered during a previous use
        val base = Config.serverUrl.toHttpUrl()
        for (text in storage.getStringSet(KEY, emptySet()).orEmpty()) {
            Cookie.parse(base, text)?.let { cookies[it.name] = it }
        }
    }

    // the response brings cookies: we store them; an expired cookie (this is
    // how the server clears the token at logout) is removed
    @Synchronized
    override fun saveFromResponse(url: HttpUrl, cookies: List<Cookie>) {
        for (c in cookies) {
            if (c.expiresAt < System.currentTimeMillis() || c.value.isEmpty()) {
                this.cookies.remove(c.name)
            } else {
                this.cookies[c.name] = c
            }
        }
        storage.edit { putStringSet(KEY, this@DeviceCookieJar.cookies.values.map { it.toString() }.toSet()) }
    }

    // a request leaves: the cookies that concern it, not expired
    @Synchronized
    override fun loadForRequest(url: HttpUrl): List<Cookie> =
        cookies.values.filter { it.expiresAt >= System.currentTimeMillis() && it.matches(url) }

    companion object {
        private const val KEY = "rdvmedecins.cookies"
    }
}

fun createHttpClient(context: Context): OkHttpClient = OkHttpClient.Builder()
    .cookieJar(DeviceCookieJar(context.getSharedPreferences("rdvmedecins", Context.MODE_PRIVATE)))
    .connectTimeout(10, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
    .readTimeout(10, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
    .build()

    The HTTP client from Example 23, and its cookie jar. Two cookies are in circulation: the token ([rdvmedecins_jwt]) and the account creation pass.

    // =========================================================================
// api/ApiError.kt - ONE class for all the errors of the API
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Taken from example 24 (common/ApiError.kt). All the error responses
// of the server have the same shape:
//   { "statusCode": 409, "key": "ERRORS.LOGIN_TAKEN", "params": {...}, "fields": {...} }
// A request without a response (network, server stopped) or a response that
// does not come from our server also become an ApiError.
// =========================================================================
package fr.stahe.rdvmedecins.api

import kotlinx.serialization.json.Json
import kotlinx.serialization.json.JsonObject
import kotlinx.serialization.json.JsonPrimitive
import kotlinx.serialization.json.jsonObject

class ApiError(
    val statusCode: Int, // 0: the server did not answer
    val key: String, // e.g. "ERRORS.LOGIN_TAKEN"
    val params: Map<String, String> = emptyMap(),
    val fields: Map<String, String> = emptyMap(),
) : Exception("$statusCode $key") {

    override fun toString() = "$statusCode $key"

    companion object {
        fun fromResponse(statusCode: Int, body: String): ApiError {
            val json = runCatching { Json.parseToJsonElement(body).jsonObject }.getOrNull()
            val key = (json?.get("key") as? JsonPrimitive)?.content
            if (json == null || key == null) {
                // no key: the proxy or the network answered instead of the server
                return ApiError(statusCode, if (statusCode >= 500) "ERRORS.SERVER_UNREACHABLE" else "ERRORS.SERVER_ERROR")
            }
            return ApiError(statusCode, key, strings(json["params"]), strings(json["fields"]))
        }

        private fun strings(json: Any?): Map<String, String> =
            (json as? JsonObject)?.mapValues { (_, v) -> (v as? JsonPrimitive)?.content ?: v.toString() } ?: emptyMap()
    }
}

    // =========================================================================
// api/ApiClient.kt - ALL the requests to the API go through here
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Taken from example 24 (common/Api.kt), with one novelty: the centralized
// handling of the 401 response.
//
// A 401 can arrive at any time: the token has expired (2 hours), the
// account has been deleted, the server has restarted with another secret
// key... Rather than handling this case in each screen, we handle it
// HERE, once. But this file knows neither the navigation nor the
// messages (it depends on nothing): it calls a function that was handed
// to it at startup (onSessionExpired, see RdvMedecinsApplication.kt),
// which forgets the user; the navigation, which observes the session, then
// goes back to the login screen.
//
// Some requests handle their 401 themselves (the login, GET
// /api/auth/me...): they are "public" (see RdvMedecinsApi.kt).
// =========================================================================
package fr.stahe.rdvmedecins.api

import fr.stahe.rdvmedecins.Config
import kotlinx.coroutines.Dispatchers
import kotlinx.coroutines.withContext
import kotlinx.serialization.json.Json
import kotlinx.serialization.json.JsonElement
import okhttp3.MediaType.Companion.toMediaType
import okhttp3.OkHttpClient
import okhttp3.Request
import okhttp3.RequestBody.Companion.toRequestBody
import java.io.IOException

class ApiClient(private val client: OkHttpClient) {
    // what to do when the server answers 401 to a protected request
    var onSessionExpired: () -> Unit = {}

    // isPublic: true for the routes that handle the 401 themselves.
    // withContext(Dispatchers.Main.immediate): the function ALWAYS ends
    // on the main thread, the screen's thread, whatever the caller's
    // thread (in an application, that is already the case: nothing
    // changes; in an instrumented test, the caller may be elsewhere). We
    // can therefore, on return, navigate or touch the state without care
    suspend fun request(method: String, url: String, body: JsonElement? = null, isPublic: Boolean = false): JsonElement? =
        withContext(Dispatchers.Main.immediate) { execute(method, url, body, isPublic) }

    private suspend fun execute(method: String, url: String, body: JsonElement?, isPublic: Boolean): JsonElement? {
        val response = withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
            val httpBody = body?.toString()?.toRequestBody("application/json".toMediaType())
            val request = Request.Builder().url("${Config.serverUrl}/api$url").method(method, httpBody).build()
            try {
                client.newCall(request).execute().use { it.code to it.body?.string().orEmpty() }
            } catch (e: IOException) {
                // no response: network down, server stopped, wrong address
                throw ApiError(0, "ERRORS.SERVER_UNREACHABLE")
            }
        }
        // destructuring of the (code, text) pair
        val (code, text) = response
        if (code >= 400) {
            val error = ApiError.fromResponse(code, text)
            if (error.statusCode == 401 && !isPublic) {
                // back on the screen's thread: we can touch the state
                onSessionExpired()
                // the screen that was waiting for the response will display THIS message too
                throw ApiError(401, "ERRORS.SESSION_EXPIRED")
            }
            throw error
        }
        return if (text.isEmpty()) null else Json.parseToJsonElement(text)
    }
}
    • lines 42–43: the function exits ALWAYS on the main thread, the screen thread ([Dispatchers.Main.immediate]): upon return, you can navigate or interact with the state without caution;
    • lines 46–53: the request, on the I/O thread (see Example 24);
    • lines 60–64: the new feature: a 401 on a protected route indicates an expired session. We handle it HERE, once for all requests: [onSessionExpired()], then an [ApiError] whose key is the message to be displayed.

    // =========================================================================
// api/Types.kt - the JSON objects exchanged with the server
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The translation, into Kotlin @Serializable classes, of the API described in
// the chapter "The server, a black box" (see common/Types.kt of the
// examples). Reading a JSON that does not have the expected shape fails
// as soon as it is received.
// =========================================================================
package fr.stahe.rdvmedecins.api

import kotlinx.serialization.Serializable
import kotlinx.serialization.json.Json
import kotlinx.serialization.json.JsonElement
import kotlinx.serialization.serializer

enum class Role { ADMIN, DOCTOR, USER }

// POST /api/auth/login, GET /api/auth/me, PUT /api/my-account
@Serializable
data class User(val login: String, val name: String, val role: Role)

// GET /api/captcha
@Serializable
data class Captcha(val id: String, val svg: String)

// a title, a first name, a last name
@Serializable
data class Identity(val title: String, val firstName: String, val lastName: String) {
    val label get() = "$title $firstName $lastName" // "Mme Alice DURAND"
}

// a doctor or a client: GET /api/doctors, GET /api/clients/:id...
@Serializable
data class Person(
    val id: Int,
    val version: Int, // optimistic lock: to be sent back with an update
    val title: String,
    val firstName: String,
    val lastName: String,
    val login: String? = null, // only for the ADMIN
) {
    val label get() = "$title $firstName $lastName"
}

// a time slot
@Serializable
data class Slot(val id: Int, val startHour: Int, val startMinute: Int, val endHour: Int, val endMinute: Int)

// a row of the schedule, with the RIGHTS of the logged-in user
@Serializable
data class ScheduleSlot(
    val id: Int,
    val startHour: Int,
    val startMinute: Int,
    val endHour: Int,
    val endMinute: Int,
    val free: Boolean,
    val patient: Identity?, // null: free, or taken by another patient
    val mine: Boolean, // the logged-in patient's appointment
    val bookable: Boolean,
    val appointmentId: Int?, // set if the user can cancel
)

// GET /api/schedule?doctorId=...&day=...
@Serializable
data class Schedule(
    val doctor: Person,
    val day: String, // "yyyy-MM-dd"
    val slots: List<ScheduleSlot>,
    val info: String?, // translation key (patient who already has an appointment)
)

// an appointment of GET /api/my-area
@Serializable
data class Appointment(val id: Int, val day: String, val slot: Slot, val doctor: Person)

// GET /api/my-area
@Serializable

inline fun <reified T> JsonElement?.read(): T =
    apiJson.decodeFromJsonElement(serializer<T>(), this ?: throw IllegalStateException("empty response"))

    // =========================================================================
// api/RdvMedecinsApi.kt - one function per route of the API
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The "data access layer" of the client (a "repository"): the screens
// call these typed functions, without knowing anything about the URLs, OkHttp or
// JSON. If the API changes, only this file changes.
// Each function is suspending; on failure, it throws an ApiError.
// The form data are simple Map<String, Any?>: their
// keys are the names of the fields expected by the server - and those of the
// errors it sends back (ApiError.fields).
// =========================================================================
package fr.stahe.rdvmedecins.api

import android.net.Uri
import kotlinx.serialization.json.JsonElement
import kotlinx.serialization.json.JsonNull
import kotlinx.serialization.json.JsonObject
import kotlinx.serialization.json.JsonPrimitive
import kotlinx.serialization.json.boolean
import kotlinx.serialization.json.jsonObject
import kotlinx.serialization.json.jsonPrimitive

// /api/doctors or /api/clients: both are handled the same way
enum class PersonType(val path: String) { DOCTORS("doctors"), CLIENTS("clients") }

typealias FormData = Map<String, Any?>

// form data -> a JSON object
fun FormData.toJson(): JsonObject = JsonObject(
    mapValues { (_, v) ->
        when (v) {
            null -> JsonNull
            is Number -> JsonPrimitive(v)
            is Boolean -> JsonPrimitive(v)
            else -> JsonPrimitive(v.toString())
        }
    },
)

class RdvMedecinsApi(private val client: ApiClient) {
    private suspend fun get(url: String, isPublic: Boolean = false) = client.request("GET", url, isPublic = isPublic)

    private suspend fun post(url: String, body: JsonElement, isPublic: Boolean = false) =
        client.request("POST", url, body, isPublic)

    // ------------------------------------------------ login (public routes)
    suspend fun captcha(): Captcha = get("/captcha", isPublic = true).read()

    suspend fun me(): User = get("/auth/me", isPublic = true).read()

    suspend fun login(login: String, password: String, captchaId: String, captcha: String): User =
        post(
            "/auth/login",
            mapOf("login" to login, "password" to password, "captchaId" to captchaId, "captcha" to captcha).toJson(),
            isPublic = true,
        ).read()

    suspend fun logout() {
        post("/auth/logout", JsonObject(emptyMap()), isPublic = true)
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------ account creation (public)
    suspend fun registrationAccess(captchaId: String, captcha: String) {
        post("/register/access", mapOf("captchaId" to captchaId, "captcha" to captcha).toJson(), isPublic = true)
    }

    suspend fun registrationAccessStatus(): Boolean =
        get("/register/access", isPublic = true)?.jsonObject?.get("valid")?.jsonPrimitive?.boolean ?: false

    // returns the login of the created account
    suspend fun register(data: FormData): String =
        post("/register", data.toJson(), isPublic = true)!!.jsonObject["login"]!!.jsonPrimitive.content

    // ------------------------------------------------ schedule and appointments
    // doctorId null: for a logged-in doctor, THEIR schedule
    suspend fun schedule(doctorId: Int?, day: String): Schedule {
        val params = Uri.Builder().appendQueryParameter("day", day).apply {
            if (doctorId != null) appendQueryParameter("doctorId", "$doctorId")
        }.build().encodedQuery
        return get("/schedule?$params").read()
    }

    suspend fun book(day: String, slotId: Int, clientId: Int?) {
        post("/appointments", buildMap { put("day", day); put("slotId", slotId); if (clientId != null) put("clientId", clientId) }.toJson())
    }

    suspend fun cancelAppointment(appointmentId: Int) {
        client.request("DELETE", "/appointments/$appointmentId")
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------ doctors and clients
    suspend fun list(type: PersonType): List<Person> = get("/${type.path}").read()

    suspend fun read(type: PersonType, id: Int): Person = get("/${type.path}/$id").read()

    suspend fun add(type: PersonType, data: FormData): Person = post("/${type.path}", data.toJson()).read()

    suspend fun update(type: PersonType, id: Int, data: FormData): Person =
        client.request("PUT", "/${type.path}/$id", data.toJson()).read()

    suspend fun delete(type: PersonType, id: Int) {
        client.request("DELETE", "/${type.path}/$id")
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------ the patient's area
    suspend fun myArea(): MyArea = get("/my-area").read()

    suspend fun myAccount(): MyAccount = get("/my-account").read()

    suspend fun updateMyAccount(data: FormData): User = client.request("PUT", "/my-account", data.toJson()).read()

    suspend fun deleteMyAccount(currentPassword: String) {
        client.request("DELETE", "/my-account", mapOf("currentPassword" to currentPassword).toJson())
    }
}
    • line 24: doctors or clients: an enumeration, with the path to the API for each;
    • lines 26–29: form data: a [Map] whose keys are the names of the fields expected by the server, converted to JSON;
    • lines 40–110: one function per route of the API, grouped by theme; the routes that handle the 401 themselves are “public.”

    // =========================================================================
// i18n/Translations.kt - the dictionaries, the current language
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Taken from example 25 (Dictionary.kt). The dictionaries
// (assets/i18n/fr.json, en.json) are those of the Vue.js, Angular,
// React and Flutter clients: same keys, same conventions ({{param}}). The server
// only sends back KEYS ("ERRORS.LOGIN_TAKEN"): it is here that they
// become text.
//   - t("KEY", mapOf("param" to value)): the text of the current language;
//   - changeLanguage("fr"): the application's OWN language (see example
//     21), remembered by Android; the activity is recreated in the new
//     language: our texts, but also those of Android (the calendar), the
//     dates and the numbers.
// =========================================================================
package fr.stahe.rdvmedecins.i18n

import android.content.Context
import androidx.appcompat.app.AppCompatDelegate
import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
import androidx.compose.runtime.staticCompositionLocalOf
import androidx.compose.ui.platform.LocalConfiguration
import androidx.compose.ui.platform.LocalContext
import androidx.core.os.LocaleListCompat
import kotlinx.serialization.json.Json
import kotlinx.serialization.json.JsonElement
import kotlinx.serialization.json.JsonObject
import kotlinx.serialization.json.JsonPrimitive

val languages = listOf("fr", "en")

class Translations(context: Context, val language: String) {
    private val root: JsonObject = context.assets.open("i18n/$language.json").bufferedReader().use {
        Json.parseToJsonElement(it.readText()) as JsonObject
    }

    // "LOGIN.TITLE" -> root["LOGIN"]["TITLE"]; null if missing
    private fun find(key: String): String? {
        var node: JsonElement? = root
        for (part in key.split('.')) node = (node as? JsonObject)?.get(part)
        return (node as? JsonPrimitive)?.takeIf { it.isString }?.content
    }

    // an unknown key is displayed as is: we immediately see what is missing
    fun t(key: String, params: Map<String, String> = emptyMap()): String {
        val text = find(key) ?: return key
        return Regex("\\{\\{(\\w+)\\}\\}").replace(text) { m -> params[m.groupValues[1]] ?: m.value }
    }
}

// the application's language: Android remembers it, and recreates the activity
fun changeLanguage(language: String) {
    AppCompatDelegate.setApplicationLocales(LocaleListCompat.forLanguageTags(language))
}

// the translations, provided to all the screens (see MainActivity.kt)
val LocalTranslations = staticCompositionLocalOf<Translations> { error("no translations provided") }

// the translations of the language of the current configuration
@Composable
fun rememberTranslations(): Translations {
    val context = LocalContext.current
    val language = LocalConfiguration.current.locales[0].language.let { if (it in languages) it else "en" }
    return remember(language) { Translations(context, language) }
}

// a shortcut, in a @Composable function: t("LOGIN.TITLE")
@Composable
fun t(key: String, params: Map<String, String> = emptyMap()): String = LocalTranslations.current.t(key, params)
    • lines 32–45: the dictionary from Example 25, with the same files as other clients;
    • lines 57–64: the translations for the current language, provided to all screens (see [MainActivity.kt]); the dictionary is re-read only if the language changes;
    • line 69: a shortcut [@Composable], [t("LOGIN.TITLE")]. Like any function [@Composable], it can only be called from within another: in an ordinary lambda (a [onClick], the [text] of a drop-down list), you must first translate it, or use [LocalTranslations.current.t(...)].

    // =========================================================================
// state/Session.kt - WHO is logged in?
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The logged-in user (or null), in a state observed by Compose
// (mutableStateOf): the screens that read it are recomposed when it
// changes, and the navigation (see navigation/Navigation.kt) observes it to
// leave a screen that is no longer allowed.
//
// The JWT token itself is NOT here: it is in a cookie, stored by
// the HTTP client. The session only keeps the DESCRIPTION of the user
// ({ login, name, role }).
//
// When the application starts, the session is empty: check() asks
// the server, only once, who is logged in (GET /api/auth/me).
// =========================================================================
package fr.stahe.rdvmedecins.state

import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import fr.stahe.rdvmedecins.api.RdvMedecinsApi
import fr.stahe.rdvmedecins.api.Role
import fr.stahe.rdvmedecins.api.User

class Session(private val api: RdvMedecinsApi) {
    var user by mutableStateOf<User?>(null)
        private set

    // true after a WANTED logout (button, account deletion);
    // false after an expired session. The navigation takes it into account
    var leftVoluntarily = false
        private set

    // the screen we wanted to see when the session expired (a route):
    // we will come back to it after logging in
    var requestedScreen: Any? = null

    // the displayed screen (a route), recorded by each protected screen
    var currentScreen: Any? = null

    // has the question "who is logged in?" already been asked?
    var checked by mutableStateOf(false)
        private set

    // only asks the server the first time
    suspend fun check() {
        if (checked) return
        user = try {
            api.me()
        } catch (e: Exception) {
            null // 401: nobody; or server unreachable
        }
        checked = true
    }

    suspend fun login(login: String, password: String, captchaId: String, captcha: String) {
        change(api.login(login, password, captchaId, captcha))
    }

    // the user has changed their name or login (PUT /api/my-account)
    fun update(u: User) = change(u)

    suspend fun logout() {
        try {
            api.logout()
        } finally {
            forget(voluntary = true) // even if the server does not answer
        }
    }

    // without asking the server anything: expired session, deleted account
    fun forget(voluntary: Boolean = false) = change(null, voluntary)

    private fun change(u: User?, voluntary: Boolean = false) {
        leftVoluntarily = voluntary
        user = u
    }
}

// what is deduced from the user: EXTENSION properties of the type
// User? (they also apply to null)
val User?.isAdmin get() = this?.role == Role.ADMIN
val User?.isPatient get() = this?.role == Role.USER

// ADMIN and DOCTOR: book and cancel the appointments of any patient
val User?.isManager get() = this?.role == Role.ADMIN || this?.role == Role.DOCTOR
    • lines 26–27: the user, an observed state: the top bar, the menu, and the navigation read it;
    • lines 31–39: what is needed to return, after a session has expired, to the screen you wanted to see;
    • lines 82–86: properties of EXTENSION of the type [User?]: they also apply to [null] ([this?.role]).

    // =========================================================================
// state/Messages.kt - the messages displayed to the user
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Same presentation as the other RdvMedecins clients:
//   - a SUCCESS is displayed at the TOP of the screen (green banner);
//   - an ERROR at the BOTTOM (pink banner), always visible.
// A message is a translation KEY (+ its parameters): it is therefore
// translated again on its own if the user changes the language.
//
// The "flash" messages: an action that ends with a change of
// screen (booking, adding a doctor...) leaves its message with
// flash(); it will be displayed on the NEXT screen, then will disappear at the
// following navigation. It is the navigation that calls newPage() at
// each change of screen (see navigation/Navigation.kt).
// =========================================================================
package fr.stahe.rdvmedecins.state

import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import fr.stahe.rdvmedecins.api.ApiError

data class Message(val key: String, val params: Map<String, String> = emptyMap())

class Messages {
    var success by mutableStateOf<Message?>(null)
        private set
    var error by mutableStateOf<Message?>(null)
        private set

    // the messages to display on the next screen
    private var pendingSuccess: Message? = null
    private var pendingError: Message? = null

    fun showSuccess(key: String, params: Map<String, String> = emptyMap()) {
        success = Message(key, params)
        error = null
    }

    fun showError(key: String, params: Map<String, String> = emptyMap()) {
        error = Message(key, params)
        success = null
    }

    fun showApiError(e: ApiError) = showError(e.key, e.params)

    fun clear() {
        success = null
        error = null
    }

    // for the NEXT screen
    fun flash(key: String, params: Map<String, String> = emptyMap(), success: Boolean = true) {
        if (success) pendingSuccess = Message(key, params) else pendingError = Message(key, params)
    }

    // a new screen: the messages of the previous one disappear, the
    // flash messages appear
    fun newPage() {
        success = pendingSuccess
        error = pendingError
        pendingSuccess = null
        pendingError = null
    }
}

    // =========================================================================
// state/Cache.kt - the data already read from the server
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The list of doctors almost never changes: no need to read it again at
// each visit of the schedule. The cache keeps the result of each read,
// under a KEY ("doctors", "schedule/1/2026-10-05"...):
//
//     val doctors = cache.read("doctors") { api.list(PersonType.DOCTORS) }
//
// returns the result already kept, or launches the read and keeps its
// result. Two simultaneous requests for the same key share the same
// read (a Deferred: a result to come). A failed read is not
// kept: the next one will try again.
// After an update, the affected keys are INVALIDATED:
// cache.invalidate("schedule"). The version property, an observed state,
// then changes: the screens that read it (even hidden under a dialog)
// read their data again. It is, in a few lines, what the
// TanStack Query library of the React client does.
// =========================================================================
package fr.stahe.rdvmedecins.state

import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableIntStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import kotlinx.coroutines.CoroutineScope
import kotlinx.coroutines.Deferred
import kotlinx.coroutines.async

class Cache(private val scope: CoroutineScope) {
    private val reads = mutableMapOf<String, Deferred<Any?>>()

    var version by mutableIntStateOf(0)
        private set

    @Suppress("UNCHECKED_CAST")
    suspend fun <T> read(key: String, load: suspend () -> T): T {
        val reading = reads.getOrPut(key) { scope.async { load() } }
        try {
            return reading.await() as T
        } catch (e: Exception) {
            // on failure, this read is forgotten (the next request will try again)
            if (reads[key] === reading) reads.remove(key)
            throw e
        }
    }

    // forgets all the keys that start with prefix, and notifies the screens
    fun invalidate(prefix: String) {
        reads.keys.removeAll { it.startsWith(prefix) }
        version++
    }

    // change of user: everything is forgotten, WITHOUT notifying (the screens of
    // the previous user are about to disappear, they must not read anything again)
    fun clear() = reads.clear()
}
    • Lines 36–39: [getOrPut]: If a read operation has already been started for this key, continue with that one; otherwise, start a new one. [async] launches a coroutine that produces a [Deferred], a result to come: two simultaneous requests are waiting ([await]) for the SAME read;
    • Lines 48–50: [invalidate]: The screens that read [version] from the key of a [LaunchedEffect] re-read their data.

// ALL the state of a screen is in its route (the doctor, the day...): the

package fr.stahe.rdvmedecins.navigation

object Screens {
    // the first screen: the time to ask the server who is logged in
    @Serializable
    object Startup

    // login: pre-filled just after the creation of an account
    @Serializable
    data class Login(val login: String = "")

    // day: as is, maybe invalid (it is checked by the screen)
    @Serializable
    data class Schedule(val doctorId: Int? = null, val day: String? = null)

    @Serializable
    data class Booking(val doctorId: Int?, val day: String, val slotId: Int)

    // the management screens of the doctors OR of the clients (ADMIN)
    @Serializable
    data class Persons(val type: PersonType)

    // id null: creation; otherwise, update
    @Serializable
    data class Person(val type: PersonType, val id: Int? = null)

    @Serializable
    object Register

    @Serializable
    object MyArea

    @Serializable
    object MyAccount
}

// the roles allowed for a protected screen (null: all the logged-in roles)
val adminRoles = setOf(Role.ADMIN)
val patientRoles = setOf(Role.USER)

// the home page of each role, just after logging in
fun home(u: User): Any = if (u.role == Role.USER) Screens.MyArea else Screens.Schedule()

    // =========================================================================
// navigation/Navigation.kt - the screens of the application and their rights
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The NavHost (see example 17) displays the screen of the current route, in the
// AppLayout (top bar, menu, messages).
//
// The GUARDS (see example 18):
//   - a protected screen is wrapped by Protected(route, roles): it is only
//     displayed for a logged-in user, with the right role (otherwise,
//     the 403 error screen);
//   - an effect observes the SESSION: a user who disappears (logout,
//     expired session) goes back to the login screen; a user who
//     appears (login) leaves the login screen for the screen requested
//     before the expiry, otherwise for the home page of their role.
// REMINDER: these checks are only a CONVENIENCE (not displaying a useless
// screen). The protection of the data is ensured by the server, which
// checks the token and the role again on EACH request.
//
// The "flash" messages: on each new screen, Messages.newPage().

// the public screens (without login)
fun isPublic(d: NavDestination) =
    d.hasRoute<Screens.Login>() || d.hasRoute<Screens.Register>() || d.hasRoute<Screens.Startup>()

// go to a screen by EMPTYING the stack: Back will not lead back to the previous screen
fun NavHostController.goTo(route: Any) {
    navigate(route) {
        popUpTo(graph.id) { inclusive = true }
        launchSingleTop = true
    }
}

@Composable
fun Navigation() {
    val nav = rememberNavController()
    val d = LocalDependencies.current
    val session = d.session
    val user = session.user

    // the flash messages: on each new screen (a new entry of the stack)
    LaunchedEffect(nav) {
        nav.currentBackStackEntryFlow.map { it.id }.distinctUntilChanged().collect { d.messages.newPage() }
    }

    // the session changes: relaunched on each change of user
    LaunchedEffect(user, session.checked) {
        if (!session.checked) return@LaunchedEffect
        val here = nav.currentBackStackEntry?.destination ?: return@LaunchedEffect
        if (user == null && !isPublic(here)) {
            // expired session: the current screen is remembered, to come back to it
            session.requestedScreen = if (session.leftVoluntarily) null else session.currentScreen
            nav.goTo(Screens.Login())
        } else if (user != null && (here.hasRoute<Screens.Login>() || here.hasRoute<Screens.Startup>())) {
            // logged in: the login screen no longer makes sense
            val target = session.requestedScreen ?: home(user)
            session.requestedScreen = null
            nav.goTo(target)
        }
    }

    AppLayout(nav) {
        NavHost(navController = nav, startDestination = Screens.Startup) {
            composable<Screens.Startup> { StartupPage(onNobody = { nav.goTo(Screens.Login()) }) }
            composable<Screens.Login> { e ->
                LoginPage(login = e.toRoute<Screens.Login>().login.take(30), onRegister = { nav.navigate(Screens.Register) })
            }
            composable<Screens.Schedule> { e ->
                val route = e.toRoute<Screens.Schedule>()
                Protected(route) {
                    SchedulePage(
                        doctorId = route.doctorId,
                        day = route.day,
                        // view another schedule: the current route is REPLACED
                        onView = { id, day ->
                            nav.navigate(Screens.Schedule(id, day)) { popUpTo<Screens.Schedule> { inclusive = true } }
                        },
                        // book: the dialog is PUSHED on top of the schedule
                        onBook = { id, day, slotId -> nav.navigate(Screens.Booking(id, day, slotId)) },
                        onMyArea = { nav.goTo(Screens.MyArea) },
                    )
                }
            }
            dialog<Screens.Booking> { e ->
                val route = e.toRoute<Screens.Booking>()
                Protected(route) { BookingDialog(route, onClose = { nav.popBackStack() }) }
            }
            composable<Screens.Persons> { e ->
                val route = e.toRoute<Screens.Persons>()
                Protected(route, adminRoles) {
                    PersonsPage(
                        type = route.type,
                        onAdd = { nav.navigate(Screens.Person(route.type)) },
                        onEdit = { id -> nav.navigate(Screens.Person(route.type, id)) },
                    )
                }
            }
            composable<Screens.Person> { e ->
                val route = e.toRoute<Screens.Person>()
                Protected(route, adminRoles) {
                    // back to the list: the form is popped
                    PersonFormPage(type = route.type, id = route.id, onList = {
                        if (!nav.popBackStack()) nav.goTo(Screens.Persons(route.type))
                    })
                }
            }
            composable<Screens.Register> {
                RegisterPage(onLogin = { login -> nav.goTo(Screens.Login(login)) })
            }
            composable<Screens.MyArea> {
                Protected(Screens.MyArea, patientRoles) {
                    PatientAreaPage(
                        onMyAccount = { nav.navigate(Screens.MyAccount) },
                        onSchedule = { id, day -> nav.navigate(Screens.Schedule(id, day)) },
                    )
                }
            }
            composable<Screens.MyAccount> {
                Protected(Screens.MyAccount, patientRoles) {
                    MyAccountPage(onMyArea = { nav.goTo(Screens.MyArea) })
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

// a protected screen: logged in, and, if roles is not null, with one of these roles
@Composable
fun Protected(route: Any, roles: Set<Role>? = null, content: @Composable () -> Unit) {
    val session = LocalDependencies.current.session
    val u = session.user ?: return // not logged in: the navigation goes back to the login
    // the displayed screen, remembered to come back to it after an expired session
    LaunchedEffect(route) { session.currentScreen = route }
    if (roles != null && u.role !in roles) {
        ErrorPage(code = 403)
    } else {
        content()
    }
}
    • lines 54–57: Go to a screen by CLEARING the stack: Back will not return to the previous screen (you do not return to the login screen after logging in);
    • lines 69–70: Flash messages: [currentBackStackEntryFlow], [Flow] for successive screens;
    • lines 74–85: THE application guard: an effect that is triggered each time the user changes. If no one is on a protected screen: upon login (retaining the current screen if the session has expired); if someone is on the login screen: to the requested screen, otherwise to the home screen for their role;
    • lines 89–113: the navigation graph, in the layout; [dialog<Screens.Booking>]: a destination displayed ON TOP OF the previous screen, which the Back button closes;
    • lines 156–164: [Protected]: not logged in, nothing (the effect above refers to the login); incorrect role, the 403 error screen.

// a menu entry: the route it leads to, the key of its label, its
// icon, and the test that says whether it is active for a given screen
class MenuEntry(val route: Any, val key: String, val icon: ImageVector, val active: (NavDestination, Any?) -> Boolean)

fun menuEntries(u: User?): List<MenuEntry> {
    if (u == null) return emptyList()
    // buildList: we fill a list, with ifs
    return buildList {
        if (u.isPatient) add(MenuEntry(Screens.MyArea, "APP.MENU_MY_AREA", Icons.Default.Home) { d, _ -> d.hasRoute<Screens.MyArea>() })
        add(MenuEntry(Screens.Schedule(), "APP.MENU_SCHEDULE", Icons.Default.DateRange) { d, _ -> d.hasRoute<Screens.Schedule>() })
        if (u.isAdmin) {
            add(MenuEntry(Screens.Persons(PersonType.DOCTORS), "APP.MENU_DOCTORS", Icons.Default.Face) { _, type -> type == PersonType.DOCTORS })
            add(MenuEntry(Screens.Persons(PersonType.CLIENTS), "APP.MENU_PATIENTS", Icons.Default.Person) { _, type -> type == PersonType.CLIENTS })
        }
        if (u.isPatient) add(MenuEntry(Screens.MyAccount, "APP.MENU_ACCOUNT", Icons.Default.AccountCircle) { d, _ -> d.hasRoute<Screens.MyAccount>() })
    }
}

@Composable
fun AppLayout(nav: NavHostController, content: @Composable () -> Unit) {
    val d = LocalDependencies.current
    val u = d.session.user
    val language = LocalTranslations.current.language
    val scope = rememberCoroutineScope()
    val entries = menuEntries(u)
    // the current screen, and the type of persons if it is a list or a form
    val entry by nav.currentBackStackEntryAsState()
    val destination = entry?.destination
    val type: PersonType? = when {
        destination?.hasRoute<Screens.Persons>() == true -> entry?.toRoute<Screens.Persons>()?.type
        destination?.hasRoute<Screens.Person>() == true -> entry?.toRoute<Screens.Person>()?.type
        else -> null
    }
    fun isActive(e: MenuEntry) = destination != null && e.active(destination, type)
    // a large screen: at least 800 dp wide
    val largeScreen = LocalConfiguration.current.screenWidthDp >= 800
    val drawer = rememberDrawerState(DrawerValue.Closed)
    var languageMenu by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }

    val page = @Composable {
        Scaffold(
            topBar = {
                TopAppBar(
                    title = { Text(t("APP.TITLE")) },
                    navigationIcon = {
                        if (u != null && !largeScreen) {
                            IconButton(onClick = { scope.launch { drawer.open() } }) { Icon(Icons.Default.Menu, contentDescription = "menu") }
                        }
                    },
                    colors = TopAppBarDefaults.topAppBarColors(
                        containerColor = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.primary,
                        titleContentColor = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onPrimary,
                        navigationIconContentColor = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onPrimary,
                        actionIconContentColor = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onPrimary,
                    ),
                    actions = {
                        // FR / EN: a menu; the activity is recreated in the new language
                        TextButton(onClick = { languageMenu = true }) {
                            Text(language.uppercase(), color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onPrimary, fontWeight = FontWeight.Bold)
                        }
                        DropdownMenu(expanded = languageMenu, onDismissRequest = { languageMenu = false }) {
                            for (l in languages) {
                                DropdownMenuItem(text = { Text(l.uppercase()) }, onClick = {
                                    languageMenu = false
                                    changeLanguage(l)
                                })
                            }
                        }
                        if (u != null) {
                            // the session is emptied; the navigation, which observes it, displays the login screen
                            IconButton(onClick = { scope.launch { runCatching { d.session.logout() } } }) {
                                Icon(Icons.AutoMirrored.Filled.ExitToApp, contentDescription = t("APP.LOGOUT"))
                            }
                        }
                    },
                )
            },
        ) { innerPadding ->
            Row(Modifier.padding(innerPadding).consumeWindowInsets(innerPadding).fillMaxSize()) {
                // on a large screen: the menu, permanently
                if (u != null && largeScreen) {
                    NavigationRail {
                        for (e in entries) {
                            NavigationRailItem(
                                selected = isActive(e),
                                onClick = { nav.goTo(e.route) },
                                icon = { Icon(e.icon, contentDescription = null) },
                                label = { Text(t(e.key)) },
                            )
                        }
                    }
                    VerticalDivider()
                }
                Column(Modifier.weight(1f).fillMaxSize().imePadding()) {
                    SuccessMessage()
                    Column(Modifier.weight(1f)) { content() }
                    ErrorPanel()
                }
            }
        }
    }

    if (u == null || largeScreen) {
        page()
    } else {
        // the drawer: only when logged in, and only on a small screen
        ModalNavigationDrawer(
            drawerState = drawer,
            drawerContent = {
                ModalDrawerSheet {
                    // the header: who is logged in
                    Column(Modifier.padding(start = 28.dp, top = 16.dp, end = 16.dp, bottom = 10.dp)) {
                        Text(u.name, style = MaterialTheme.typography.titleMedium)
                        SuggestionChip(onClick = {}, label = { Text(u.role.name) })
                    }
                    for (e in entries) {
                        NavigationDrawerItem(
                            label = { Text(t(e.key)) },
                            icon = { Icon(e.icon, contentDescription = null) },
                            selected = isActive(e),
                            onClick = {
                                scope.launch { drawer.close() }
                                nav.goTo(e.route)
                            },
                            modifier = Modifier.padding(horizontal = 12.dp),
                        )
                    }
                }
            },
        ) { page() }
    }
}

// the success message, at the top
@Composable
private fun SuccessMessage() {
    val messages = LocalDependencies.current.messages
    val success = messages.success ?: return
    ListItem(
        colors = ListItemDefaults.colors(containerColor = Color(0xFFE8F5E9)),
        leadingContent = { Icon(Icons.Default.CheckCircle, contentDescription = null, tint = Color(0xFF2E7D32)) },
        headlineContent = { Text(t(success.key, success.params), color = Color(0xFF1B5E20)) },
        trailingContent = { IconButton(onClick = { messages.clear() }) { Icon(Icons.Default.Close, contentDescription = null) } },
    )
}

// the error panel, at the bottom: always visible, even if the screen scrolls
@Composable
private fun ErrorPanel() {
    val messages = LocalDependencies.current.messages
    val error = messages.error ?: return
    ListItem(
        colors = ListItemDefaults.colors(containerColor = Color(0xFFF8D7DA)),
        leadingContent = { Icon(Icons.Default.Warning, contentDescription = null, tint = Color(0xFFC62828)) },
        headlineContent = { Text(t(error.key, error.params), color = Color(0xFFB71C1C)) },
        trailingContent = { IconButton(onClick = { messages.clear() }) { Icon(Icons.Default.Close, contentDescription = null) } },
    )
}

    // =========================================================================
// widgets/InputField.kt - a complete form field
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Label + field + help message OR error message. All the
// forms of the application use it:
//
//   InputField(label = "PERSONS.LASTNAME_LABEL", maxLength = 20,
//              value = input["lastName"], onChange = { update("lastName", it) },
//              error = submit.errors["lastName"])
//
// It is a CONTROLLED component (see example 11): the value belongs to the
// parent form. label, help and error are translation KEYS;
// params, the parameters of their messages ({{min}}...).
// =========================================================================
package fr.stahe.rdvmedecins.widgets

import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.fillMaxWidth
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.padding
import androidx.compose.foundation.text.KeyboardOptions
import androidx.compose.material3.OutlinedTextField
import androidx.compose.material3.Text
import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
import androidx.compose.ui.Modifier
import androidx.compose.ui.autofill.ContentType
import androidx.compose.ui.semantics.contentType
import androidx.compose.ui.semantics.semantics
import androidx.compose.ui.text.input.KeyboardType
import androidx.compose.ui.text.input.PasswordVisualTransformation
import androidx.compose.ui.text.input.VisualTransformation
import androidx.compose.ui.unit.dp
import fr.stahe.rdvmedecins.i18n.t

@Composable
fun InputField(
    label: String,
    value: String,
    onChange: (String) -> Unit,
    error: String? = null,
    help: String? = null,
    params: Map<String, String> = emptyMap(),
    secret: Boolean = false, // a password: hidden characters
    maxLength: Int? = null,
    // for the phone's password manager (username, password...)
    autofillType: ContentType? = null,
) {
    val errorMessage = error?.let { t(it, params) }
    val helpMessage = help?.let { t(it, params) }
    OutlinedTextField(
        value = value,
        // the field refuses the extra characters
        onValueChange = { v -> if (maxLength == null || v.length <= maxLength) onChange(v) },
        label = { Text(t(label)) },
        singleLine = true,
        isError = errorMessage != null,
        // the error, otherwise the help
        supportingText = (errorMessage ?: helpMessage)?.let { m -> { Text(m) } },
        visualTransformation = if (secret) PasswordVisualTransformation() else VisualTransformation.None,
        keyboardOptions = KeyboardOptions(keyboardType = if (secret) KeyboardType.Password else KeyboardType.Text),
        modifier = Modifier
            .fillMaxWidth()
            .padding(bottom = 4.dp)
            .semantics { if (autofillType != null) contentType = autofillType },
    )
}

// widgets/PersonFields.kt - title, first name, last name
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The identity fields, common to three forms: the ADMIN's doctor / client,
// "Create a patient account" and "Manage my account". The parent passes it
// the values, the errors, and the function that updates a field:
//     PersonFields(values = input, errors = submit.errors, onChange = ::update)
// =========================================================================
package fr.stahe.rdvmedecins.widgets

import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.width
import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
import androidx.compose.ui.Modifier
import androidx.compose.ui.unit.dp
import fr.stahe.rdvmedecins.i18n.t

val titles = listOf("Mr", "Mme", "Melle")

@Composable
fun PersonFields(values: Map<String, Any?>, errors: Map<String, String>, onChange: (String, String) -> Unit) {
    Column {
        DropdownList(
            label = t("PERSONS.TITLE_LABEL"),
            value = values["title"] as String,
            choices = titles,
            onChange = { onChange("title", it) },
            error = errors["title"]?.let { t(it) },
            modifier = Modifier.width(180.dp),
        )
        InputField(
            label = "PERSONS.FIRSTNAME_LABEL",
            maxLength = 20,
            value = values["firstName"] as String,
            onChange = { onChange("firstName", it) },
            error = errors["firstName"],
        )
        InputField(
            label = "PERSONS.LASTNAME_LABEL",
            maxLength = 20,
            value = values["lastName"] as String,
            onChange = { onChange("lastName", it) },
            error = errors["lastName"],
        )
    }
}

    // =========================================================================
// widgets/FormSubmit.kt - sending a form to the server
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// All the forms of the application follow the same pattern as
// example 25: no rule is checked on the phone (they live
// in ONE single place, the server), and in case of refusal:
//   - the error of each field (ApiError.fields) is displayed under the field;
//   - the general message (ApiError.key) is displayed at the bottom of the screen.
// This class groups these actions (it is the Command of example 23,
// completed with the errors of the fields). A screen creates one per form:
//
//     val submit = remember { FormSubmit(messages) }
//     if (submit.send { api.register(input) }) { ... }
//     InputField(..., error = submit.errors["lastName"])
// =========================================================================
package fr.stahe.rdvmedecins.widgets

import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateOf
import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
import fr.stahe.rdvmedecins.api.ApiError
import fr.stahe.rdvmedecins.state.Messages

class FormSubmit(private val messages: Messages) {
    // the error of each field: a translation KEY
    var errors by mutableStateOf(mapOf<String, String>())
        private set

    // the parameters of the error messages ({{min}}...), sent back by the server
    var params by mutableStateOf(mapOf<String, String>())
        private set
    var inProgress by mutableStateOf(false)
        private set

    // runs the submission; returns true if it succeeded. In case of ApiError, the
    // errors are displayed and false is returned
    suspend fun send(action: suspend () -> Unit): Boolean {
        if (inProgress) return false // no double submission
        errors = emptyMap()
        params = emptyMap()
        inProgress = true
        try {
            action()
            return true
        } catch (e: ApiError) {
            messages.showApiError(e)
            errors = e.fields
            params = e.params
            return false
        } finally {
            inProgress = false
        }
    }

    // the user changes a field: its error disappears
    fun clearError(field: String) {
        if (field in errors) errors = errors - field
    }
}

    The [Command] from Example 23, with field errors added: all forms in the application use it.
